translation: They say that when the qi of water is replete it must be able to control fire, and when vacuous it cannot control fire; hence yang repletion and yin vacuity cause heat and dryness to dry up the fluids, and the urine is dribbling and constantly scanty; yin repletion and yang vacuity cannot control water, and the urine is free-flowing and constantly copious. How would they know that in wasting-thirst with much urination, it is not this that is meant? Why? Because dryness-heat is excessive, and the interstices (腠理) of the three burners, intestines, and stomach become depressed, knotted, and stagnant, dense, and obstructed, so that the water and fluids cannot be discharged to moisten and infiltrate the exterior and nourish the hundred bones. Hence outside the intestines and stomach, dryness-heat is excessive; even though one drinks much within, in the end it cannot moisten and infiltrate the exterior, hence the thirst does not cease. The urine is passed in great quantity because, with much drinking, [the water] cannot seep and drain out to the exterior of the intestines and stomach, hence there is frequent urination.
translator_notes: 腠理 rendered as interstices (standard term).
